A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TT-TFHE, with matching core methods and experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, inference-time and resource measurements on Adult, Cancer, Diabetes, MNIST and CIFAR-10, plus lookup-table timing experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark measurements and adds XGBoost comparisons, CIFAR-10 ablations and deployment-cost analyses.

M1.justification: v1 splits the final linear regression between server and client to accommodate Concrete's uniform precision restriction. v2 supports multiprecision computation and specifies splitting only when suitable cryptographic parameters cannot be found. This changes inference procedure, while the core LTT architectures and training approach remain.

E1.justification: Both versions document experiments on Adult, Cancer, Diabetes, MNIST and CIFAR-10 with the same classification tasks. v2 Section 5.2.3 adds explicitly projected ImageNet results, rather than documenting an executed ImageNet experiment. The preprocessing variants and hypothetical customer counts change protocols rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated XGBoost baselines at six-bit and four-bit precision, additional Zama configurations, DCT-CryptoNets and Rovida et al. across its performance, memory and cost comparisons. These substantially expand comparator coverage. ETHZ/CCS22 in v1 is the retained Jovanovic et al. (2022) comparator, not a new method.

E3.justification: v2 distinguishes Full-Pr from client-preprocessed epsilon settings and reports separate tabular results; the earlier Full-Pr MNIST configuration is reclassified. Adult's documented inputs change from 18 binary attributes to 14 original features encoded into 94 binary and six numerical features, without establishing a rerun. New protocols include first-100-image error tests and a 100,000-request cost model. Zama RAM measurement also moves from Colab to the authors' workstation.

E4.justification: New Appendix E substantially extends the existing bitwidth comparison with 16-bit truth tables, alternative linear-regression precisions, FHE error-probability tests and a split-versus-unsplit regression comparison. Tables 10–11 examine accuracy, latency, memory and communication tradeoffs. v1's brief built-in-versus-ad-hoc regression finding is removed.

E5.justification: Both dataset appendices report five 80/20 train-test splits. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The new FHE error-probability ablation concerns computational error tolerance, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported VGG1B/TT MNIST time changes from 7 to 4.4 seconds at 98.1% accuracy. CIFAR-10 timings change from 9.5 minutes/6.2 hours to 8.7 minutes/1 hour for the retained four-/six-bit configurations. Resource measurements also change substantially, and v2 adds Full-Pr tabular, baseline, ablation, cost and projected ImageNet results. These accompany implementation and setting revisions, so they do not establish uniformly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: The binarization formula, truth-table construction and linear-regression bit decomposition remain mathematically unchanged. v2 adds explanatory background, including Quine–McCluskey optimization, but no new proof, theorem or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 elevates deployment economics into an explicit contribution and adds an abstract/introduction claim of cost reductions by one to several orders of magnitude. v1 emphasizes accuracy, latency, memory and practical deployment without this quantitative economic claim. The original framework and privacy claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the blanket lack-of-multiprecision limitation with conditional cryptographic-parameter feasibility and interprets regression splitting as a latency-versus-memory/communication tradeoff. It explains the substantial cost of server-side tabular preprocessing and recommends epsilon settings for deployment. It also adds qualifications about CKKS amortized-runtime comparisons and adapting quantized rule models.

D1.justification: v2 specifies Concrete 2.10.0 and adds preprocessing placement, XGBoost precision settings, ablation controls and deployment-cost inputs. The earlier patchwise-compilation explanation disappears. Most architecture descriptions, training information, hardware details and dataset access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references and discussion covering newer Zama work, DCT-CryptoNets, Rovida and Leporati, GLRM, model extraction and an FHE survey. Its positioning around automated TTnet-to-TFHE inference largely remains. The TTnet preprint-to-IJCAI citation update represents the same antecedent work.

P1.justification: v2 edits and expands explanatory prose, moves TTnet background into a standalone section before the framework, and integrates the former memory appendix into the main results. Appendix headings, terminology and author information also change. Much of the retained narrative and wording remains intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with substantially reorganized tables. v2 adds a settings recap, cost tables and ablation tables; splits and relocates resource tables; and integrates normalized tabular timings into the main comparison. The existing diagrams are retained, with Figures 1 and 2 exchanging order.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, v2 adds useful baselines, controlled ablations and clearer preprocessing distinctions. However, its new headline cost claims depend on inconsistent entries: Adult epsilon/TT RAM is 13.6 MB in Table 4 but 3.4 MB in Table 7, and Table 7's Diabetes costs of $17.7 versus $0.06 imply about 295-fold savings rather than the reported 558-fold. These unresolved discrepancies prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite the useful additions.
